ru-1-1.text: Customer focus. How are customer requirements, risks, and opportunities taken into account? How is commitment to enhancing customer satisfaction maintained?

ru-1-2.text: Is the organizational structure approved, process owners identified, and are roles and responsibilities assigned?
ru-1-2.examples: Expected evidence: Organizational chart; process model (landscape).

ru-1-3.text: Are risks and opportunities identified when planning the QMS, and have actions been taken to address them?
ru-1-3.examples: Expected evidence: Risk register and records of risk treatment actions.
docs: Risk register and records of risk treatment actions

ru-1-4.text: Has a quality policy been developed and communicated to personnel, taking customer requirements into account?
ru-1-4.examples: Expected evidence: Quality policy and records of communication/awareness.
docs: Quality policy and records of communication/awareness

ru-1-5.text: Are defect-level targets defined (with a defined method for assessing defect level) for the plant over a three-year horizon, and are they achieved? Does the organization monitor defect levels internally, at customers, and at suppliers?
ru-1-5.examples: Expected evidence: Objectives and monitoring data.

ru-1-6.text: Is planning and monitoring in place for achieving objectives in quality, occupational health and safety, and environmental management (where applicable)?
ru-1-6.examples: Expected evidence: Objectives and monitoring data.

ru-1-7.text: Have KPIs been defined for each process?
ru-1-7.examples: Expected evidence: Objectives and monitoring data.

ru-1-8.text: Have external and internal issues that are relevant to the organization’s context and strategic direction been determined? Is information on interested parties tracked and analyzed?

ru-1-9.text: Have the processes required for the QMS been determined?
ru-1-9.examples: Expected evidence: Process descriptions (e.g. turtle diagram).

ru-1-10.text: Is documented information defined to support process operation and control?

ru-1-11.text: Do process performance indicators reflect customer requirements?
ru-1-11.examples: Expected evidence: Objectives and monitoring; customer requirements.

ru-1-12.text: When process targets are not met, are corrective actions developed?
ru-1-12.examples: Expected evidence: Objectives and corrective actions.

ru-1-13.text: Are rules established for conducting audits (QMS, process, and product audits)?
ru-1-13.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity, with a sample record.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-1-14.text: Internal audit: planning, execution, and follow-up monitoring.
ru-1-14.examples: Expected evidence: Approved audit schedule and monitoring records.
docs: Approved audit schedule and monitoring records

ru-1-15.text: Is competence of internal auditors demonstrated and on file?
ru-1-15.examples: Expected evidence: Competence matrix and supporting evidence.

ru-1-16.text: Is the organization certified to ISO 9001 or IATF 16949, and to ISO 14001 / ISO 45001 where applicable?

ru-1-17.text: Are MMOG/LE requirements implemented, and is an annual self-assessment performed?
ru-1-17.examples: Expected evidence: Per supply agreement (self-assessment submitted to customer by 1 February each year, if required).
docs: Supply agreement and annual self-assessment submission records (e.g. to customer by 1 February)

ru-1-18.text: Legislative and regulatory requirements applicable to the organization’s products and processes.
ru-1-18.examples: Expected evidence: Register of applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
docs: Register of applicable legal and regulatory requirements

ru-1-19.examples: Expected evidence: Supplier evaluation / customer feedback records.

ru-1-20.examples: Expected evidence: Top management review records.

ru-1-21.text: Is a continual improvement and cost-reduction system in place? How many initiatives were implemented in the last year and how effective were they?
ru-1-21.examples: Expected evidence: Improvement proposals, kaizen, employee suggestions.

ru-2-1.text: Is a documented process in place defining requirements for production readiness projects for new products and product changes?

ru-2-2.text: Are production readiness projects implemented in line with APQP or ANPQP?
ru-2-2.examples: Expected evidence: Documented information where these requirements are specified.
docs: Documented information where these requirements are specified

ru-2-3.text: Is up-to-date product-defining documentation available (drawings, technical specifications, national standards, etc.)?
ru-2-3.examples: Expected evidence: Customer-specific APQP/PPAP package folder for the project.

ru-2-4.text: Have key product characteristics and related requirements been defined and agreed with the customer (PPM, Cpk, Ppk, special characteristics as applicable)?
ru-2-4.examples: Expected evidence: Special-characteristics chart or equivalent.

ru-2-5.text: Have key characteristics of materials and purchased components, and related requirements, been defined and agreed with suppliers (PPM, Cpk, Ppk, special characteristics as applicable)?

ru-2-6.text: Is production readiness managed as a project (schedule with assigned responsibilities)?
ru-2-6.examples: Expected evidence: Production readiness schedule (e.g. customer SMS/milestone schedule).

ru-2-7.text: Is there a prototype and pilot-lot test plan (characteristics, test volume, test methods) for all products in scope?
ru-2-7.examples: Expected evidence: Test plan, test report, and test results.

ru-2-8.text: Are results available from prototype and pilot-lot testing?
ru-2-8.examples: Expected evidence: Test plan, test report, and test results.

ru-2-9.text: Is Design FMEA used to evaluate the design?
ru-2-9.examples: Expected evidence: Standard describing the activity and the DFMEA.

ru-2-10.text: Are process flow diagrams, control plans, and Process FMEA used to develop and assess the manufacturing process?
ru-2-10.examples: Expected evidence: Standard describing the activity; process flow, control plan, PFMEA.

ru-2-11.text: Are process flow diagrams, control plans, and PFMEA consistent with each other?

ru-2-12.text: Are layout decisions for warehouse and production areas reviewed on a planned basis as part of the production readiness project?
ru-2-12.examples: Expected evidence: Approved layout considering the new project.
docs: Approved layout considering the new project

ru-2-13.text: Is customer production approval performed in accordance with PPAP requirements and PSW?
ru-2-13.examples: Expected evidence: Documented information defining required submission documents.
docs: Documented information defining required submission documents

ru-2-14.text: Are product safety requirements identified and implemented?
ru-2-14.examples: Expected evidence: Material/product technical safety requirements.

ru-2-15.text: Is phase-gate control applied alongside the master schedule; are meeting minutes available; does a responsible person issue a gate decision per the standard?
ru-2-15.examples: Expected evidence: Phase audits, meeting minutes, gate decision/conclusion.

ru-2-16.text: Is there a list of substances prohibited in design and production, agreed with the customer and meeting environmental requirements? Is there test evidence confirming absence of these substances?
ru-2-16.examples: Expected evidence: Material composition report or equivalent.

ru-2-17.text: Are prohibited-substance requirements communicated to suppliers? Is there test evidence confirming absence of these substances?
ru-2-17.examples: Expected evidence: Documented activity; test report.

ru-2-18.text: Is registration completed on the IMDS portal (www.mdsystem.com) where required?

ru-3-1.text: Is tooling identified, are passports/dossiers maintained, and is information kept current?
ru-3-1.examples: Expected evidence: Tooling identification (number, name, or equivalent).

ru-3-2.text: Is tooling status identification implemented: serviceable, maintenance/repair required, or mothballed?
ru-3-2.examples: Expected evidence: Tooling status indicator (e.g. traffic-light system).

ru-3-3.text: Is tooling stored in a manner that prevents damage?
ru-3-3.examples: Expected evidence: Storage requirements (rack, trolley, or equivalent).

ru-3-4.text: Are criteria defined for tooling qualification (initial, periodic, and after repair)?
ru-3-4.examples: Expected evidence: Tooling ID with last qualification date and next due date.
docs: Tooling ID with last qualification date and next due date

ru-3-5.text: For multi-cavity tooling, is qualification performed using parts from each cavity/stream (where applicable)?
ru-3-5.examples: Expected evidence: Demonstrate measurement for each cavity/stream.

ru-3-6.text: Are current drawings available for all tooling (where applicable)?

ru-3-7.text: Are preventive maintenance schedules in place for all equipment and tooling (where applicable)?
ru-3-7.examples: Expected evidence: Approved preventive maintenance schedules and monitoring records.

ru-3-8.text: Are planned maintenance and servicing activities for equipment and tooling clearly defined (where applicable)?
ru-3-8.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-3-9.text: Are logs maintained for planned and breakdown maintenance, including failure records (paper or IT system)?
ru-3-9.examples: Expected evidence: Maintenance logs or system records.

ru-3-10.text: Are records kept of maintenance work performed and acceptance of repairs?

ru-3-11.text: Is there a process to adjust preventive maintenance plans based on breakdown maintenance data?
ru-3-11.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-3-12.text: Is overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) or equivalent equipment utilization assessed?
ru-3-12.examples: Expected evidence: OEE or utilization assessment records.

ru-3-13.text: On what criteria is key/critical equipment defined?
ru-3-13.examples: Expected evidence: Spare parts list for key equipment.
docs: Spare parts list for key equipment

ru-3-14.text: Are stock levels defined for spare parts for key equipment, and are target levels met?
ru-3-14.examples: Expected evidence: Physical count vs spare parts list.
docs: Physical count vs spare parts list

ru-4-1.text: Has the organization determined staffing levels needed for stable operations?
ru-4-1.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-4-2.text: Is employee turnover monitored and managed?
ru-4-2.examples: Expected evidence: Objectives, monitoring, and preventive actions are defined and tracked.

ru-4-3.text: Are competence requirements defined for each workstation?
ru-4-3.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-4-4.text: Are criteria defined for qualification and re-qualification of operators to perform each operation?
ru-4-4.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-4-5.text: Are records maintained for operator qualification?

ru-4-6.text: Are induction/onboarding plans in place for new employees?
ru-4-6.examples: Expected evidence: Standard or procedure describing the activity.
docs: Standard or procedure describing the activity

ru-4-7.text: Are job descriptions established and aligned with the qualification matrix?

ru-4-8.text: Is a visible skills matrix maintained showing qualification levels per workstation?
